changelog: Completed the Candidate Site flow so map clicks can be inspected, enriched with modeled light-pollution data, and saved as normal observation Sites.
Added modeled Light Pollution data to Site details, clearly separating estimated Falchi/New World Atlas values from manual or measured sky-quality fields.

Added Update light pollution data for existing Sites so older locations can fetch or refresh modeled SQM, Bortle, artificial brightness, ratio, total brightness, dataset, source, and update timestamp.
Polished Candidate Site and Create Site UX with clearer SQM/Bortle emphasis, read-only light-pollution previews, fallback messaging, and default names based on coordinates.
Added Current Device Position for field recon, including geolocation states, accuracy display, a temporary device marker, and Inspect this location handoff into the existing Candidate Site workflow.
Added Local Horizon Profile v1 for Sites with manual azimuth/min-altitude points, validation, persistence, editor modal, template generation, clearing, and compass visualization.
Integrated Local Horizon with Conditions so target visibility, hourly rows, limiting factors, and Observing Window now account for active Site obstructions when a horizon profile is configured.
Added LP-4 local raster point lookup for Candidate Site light-pollution data using a configurable New World Atlas / Falchi 2016 GeoTIFF.

Added a backend /api/light-pollution endpoint that validates WGS84 coordinates, reads a single raster cell, handles missing datasets, nodata, and out-of-bounds points, and returns normalized TSN DSS data.
Separated the visual ArcGIS ArtificialSkyBrightness overlay from the local raster point-data provider so map rendering and point values can evolve independently.
Reused TSN DSS light-pollution conversions for artificial brightness, artificial/natural ratio, estimated total brightness, estimated SQM, and estimated Bortle class.
Updated Candidate Site popups to display New World Atlas/Falchi source metadata and a clear dataset-unavailable state when the local raster is not configured.
Extended the Horizon Compass with a Moon trajectory using hourly Moon Alt/Az data from Astronomical Conditions.
Added smaller Moon points and subtle below-horizon points for both the target and Moon so hidden portions of each path remain visible without dominating the compass.
Reworked Target visibility into a narrower one-column metric panel so the Horizon Compass can use more horizontal space.
Limited compass trajectory rendering to the day containing the selected observing window, while keeping the observing window highlighted as the brighter path.
Kept a 24-hour compass fallback when no observing window is available.
Changed the Conditions range control from hours to days and wired Open-Meteo requests to use forecast_days up to the 16-day API range.
Kept astronomical Conditions timeline requests hour-based internally by deriving forecast_hours from the selected number of forecast days.
Reworked Observation Center site selection into a top horizontal site bar with Create site aligned on the right.
Simplified Conditions so it uses the active site from Observation Center and can use the full workspace width without an extra site selector.
Rebuilt Sites into a cleaner details-and-map layout with site data on the left, the map on the right, and Create/Edit site handled through modal dialogs.
Fixed modal layering above the Leaflet map and cleaned redundant site/map header metadata from the Sites view.
Added a configurable forecast-range slider to Conditions and wired it to reload both weather and astronomical snapshots for the active site.
Expanded observing-window handling so Conditions can expose multiple windows across the selected time range and let the user switch the active window.
Added a Horizon Compass to Target visibility, showing the current target direction from Alt/Az together with a human-readable field orientation summary.
Extended the Horizon Compass with the target trajectory across the visible sky, including hourly points, observing-window highlighting, and hover-based time details.
Refined the Conditions layout by removing redundant summary sections and making observing-window cues more prominent, including short-window fallbacks on the compass.
Color-coded the hourly Conditions table so day, twilight, astronomical night, and the active observing window are easier to scan at a glance.
Extended MosaicPlan with optional observation_type and filter fields so observing intent can be stored at the plan level without breaking existing mosaics.
Added MosaicPlan create, read, and update support for the new intent fields across SQLite persistence, the local API, and the Sky mosaic editor UI.
Expanded Conditions with context-aware observing-condition assessment driven by Moon, dew, wind, and gusts inside the current observing window.
Added an overall GOOD / MODERATE / POOR assessment beside the observing window while keeping the detailed factor-by-factor assessment as an explainability layer.
Added a new Astronomical Conditions layer beside weather, with normalized Sun, Moon, twilight, and astronomical-night data for the active observing site.
Extended Observation Center Conditions with target-aware altitude, azimuth, airmass, transit, Moon separation, and night visibility windows derived from the selected mosaic panel or planned pointing.
Added a new local astronomical-conditions API endpoint and kept provider-specific astronomy logic behind the backend instead of leaking library structures into the frontend.
Extended Observation Center Conditions with astronomy-relevant Open-Meteo fields including dew point, visibility, surface pressure, layered cloud cover, weather code, and day/night state.
Added TSN DSS dew-margin and dew-risk calculations so forecast data now includes local interpretation for condensation risk.
Kept weather provider mapping behind the local API and expanded the Conditions UI to emphasize the values most useful for observing decisions.
Added hardware-agnostic telescope adapter selection, including the first Seestar-facing adapter skeleton beside the simulator.
Introduced the first mosaic planning flow in Sky, with panel generation, panel selection, and planned-pointing handoff to telescope control.
Reworked the Sky workspace into one shared map with separate Telescope control and Mosaic planner tabs.
Expanded the header with hardware status and kept the frontend aligned with the shared telescope-state model.
Completed a repository cleanup pass: refreshed docs, documented core Python and frontend modules, narrowed top-level exports, and moved active plans into docs/plans.
Added Sky simulator controls for manual telescope state updates directly from the map workspace.
Rendered the telescope marker and imaging footprint in Aladin from the shared telescope state model.
Stopped Update telescope from resetting the current zoom level in the Sky view.
Added a Follow telescope toggle so the map can either stay fixed or track the telescope position on demand.
Improved telescope movement behavior so the marker shifts on the map without forcing a full view recenter in the default mode.
Reworked Projects into a gallery-first layout with a dedicated left selection column for captures and runs.
Merged the project preview and edited outputs into a single unified gallery, with the preview shown as the first gallery item.
Rebuilt Import Capture to use the same left-sidebar plus right-gallery layout as Projects.
Reorganized Processing into the same workspace pattern, with Create Run, capture selection, run selection, and a wider detail area.
Simplified Sky into a focused map-only workspace and removed the extra context and planning tabs.
Moved Core content into a versioned JSON source and updated the Core page to show the latest release expanded with older releases collapsed below.
SQLite foundation, schema versioning, and integrity tests are in place.
Project storage supports isolated captures, runs, and Siril workspaces.
OSC_Preprocessing can be launched headless through the Siril CLI.
Processing runs persist logs, status, output FITS, and generated previews.
The GUI now has dedicated workspaces for Core, Projects, Processing, and Sky.
The capture browser uses cached thumbnails instead of full-size image loads.
